md_description: This workflow captures coral reef microbial community sampling from multiple Great Barrier Reef sites and depths, records in situ environmental conditions, sequences 16S rRNA gene amplicons, and computes microbial community profiles for downstream analysis. It integrates environmental metadata with sequencing-derived community tables to support interpretation of spatial heterogeneity, coral health, and resilience-related microbial patterns.

coral_reef_site_samples.reasoning: For the Entity node coral_reef_site_samples, I included only intrinsic sample identity and origin descriptors: where the samples came from, what reef compartment they represent, and the spatial context needed to distinguish collections across sites and depths. I excluded preservation, extraction, sequencing, environmental measurements, and any file/data outputs because those belong to downstream Process, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. I also avoided duplicating later fields such as environmental metadata, raw reads, or community tables, and did not repeat generic sample identifiers unless needed as the primary entity identifier for this node.

md_schema.descr: Primary identifier for each collected reef sample; use a stable string such as 'GBR_S01_D10m_A' that uniquely labels the sampling unit within the dataset. Assigned at collection time and used to link this Entity to downstream preservation and molecular-processing steps.
Name of the Great Barrier Reef collection site where the sample was obtained; record the site designation used in the field log or cruise metadata, e.g. 'Lizard Island', 'Heron Island'.
Short site code used operationally to label the collection location; use the exact code recorded during sampling, e.g. 'LIZ_03' or 'HER_02'.
Water depth at which the sample was collected, in meters below the sea surface; record the in situ depth associated with the sample at collection, typically 0.5 to 30 m for reef transects.

Free-text description of the local collection position within the reef system, such as reef flat, reef slope, back reef, lagoon, or fore reef; capture the spatial microhabitat context at the time of sampling.

Physical material collected for microbial community analysis; specify the reef sample matrix represented by the entity, such as seawater, mucus-associated material, biofilm, or sediment if applicable to this dataset.
Date the reef sample was collected in the field, recorded at the time of sampling in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD), e.g. 2024-07-18.

Brief description of how the sample was obtained in the field, limited to the sampling action itself rather than preservation or processing; examples include 'sterile bottle grab', 'syringe filtration', or 'swab collection'.
Replicate index for samples collected at the same site and depth, if multiple biological or technical field replicates were taken; use integers such as 1, 2, 3.

Immediate observable condition of the sample at the time it was collected, if recorded; use a simple categorical label describing the field state, not preservation or quality metrics from later steps.

sample_preservation.reasoning: For the Process node sample_preservation, I included only preservation protocol parameters and operator-controlled stabilization details: preservative used, storage temperature, timing, duration, and any transport/cold-chain conditions that directly define how preservation was performed. I excluded intrinsic sample origin fields because those belong to the upstream Entity, and I excluded downstream DNA quality, extraction yield, or file/data properties because those belong to later Entity/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating sample identifiers already generated for the Entity node and kept the schema limited to process-level factors needed to reproduce the preservation step.

md_schema.descr: Primary preservation approach applied immediately after reef sample collection to stabilize microbial DNA prior to extraction; record the method used in this workflow, e.g. 'flash_freezing', 'dna_stabilizing_buffer', 'ethanol_preservation', or 'refrigerated_hold'.

Name of the chemical preservative or stabilization reagent used during sample preservation, if applicable; record the reagent exactly as used in the field or lab, e.g. 'RNAlater', 'ethanol', or 'no_reagent'.

Volume of preservative added to each sample during preservation, in milliliters; record the amount applied at the time of stabilization, typically 0.5 to 50 mL depending on sample type and container size.
Elapsed time from sample collection to initiation of preservation, in minutes; record this interval at the point preservation begins, typically ranging from 0 to 120 minutes in field workflows.
Total time the sample remained under the preservation condition before downstream processing or transfer, in hours; record the duration of the stabilization hold, typically 0.5 to 168 hours.
Temperature used for preservation storage or transport, in degrees Celsius, measured or set during the preservation step; examples include -80, -20, 4, or ambient depending on protocol.

Controlled transport condition maintained after preservation and before extraction; use the operational state applied to the preserved sample, such as 'on_ice', 'dry_ice', 'frozen_shipping', or 'ambient_short_term'.

Process-level flag indicating whether the preservation step met the intended protocol requirements at the end of the step; use this to record deviations such as temperature excursions or delayed stabilization that could affect DNA integrity.

preserved_samples.reasoning: For the Entity node preserved_samples, I included only intrinsic post-preservation state descriptors of the sample itself, such as preservation state, storage state, and integrity/status attributes that define what the sample is after the preservation process. I excluded collection-origin fields already assigned to the upstream sample entity, and I did not include extraction, sequencing, or file-related descriptors because those belong to downstream process, signal, or derivative nodes. I also avoided duplicating any identifiers already generated upstream, keeping this node focused on the preserved material as an entity ready for molecular processing.

md_schema.descr: State of the sample after the field preservation step; use a categorical label describing whether the sample has been successfully stabilized for downstream molecular processing, e.g. 'preserved', 'partially_preserved', or 'compromised'.

Current storage condition of the preserved sample entity after preservation and before extraction; record the state as maintained for downstream handling, such as frozen, chilled, or buffered storage.

Container or vessel type holding the preserved sample after field stabilization, such as a cryovial, sterile tube, or filtered cartridge housing; record the physical storage container used before extraction.

Approximate volume or amount of preserved sample material retained after field stabilization, in milliliters; record this as the sample amount available for downstream molecular processing, typically applicable to liquid reef samples.

Subjective or scored indicator of sample condition after preservation and before extraction, reflecting whether the preserved material appears intact and usable for DNA work; use a simple categorical assessment recorded at receipt or transfer.

dna_extraction.reasoning: For the Process node dna_extraction, I included only extraction protocol details and operator-controlled settings: extraction kit/chemistry, lysis approach, input amount, elution conditions, and extraction yield/purity as process outcome indicators. I excluded preserved-sample identity, storage, and container fields because those belong to the upstream Entity, and I excluded downstream library, sequencing, and read properties because those belong to later nodes. I also avoided repeating any sample identifiers already generated and stayed within the process territory by describing how microbial DNA was obtained from the preserved reef samples, not what the DNA entity itself is beyond its extraction output.

md_schema.descr: Commercial kit or in-house chemistry used to extract microbial DNA from preserved reef samples; record the exact kit name used for this step, e.g. 'DNeasy PowerSoil Pro Kit' or equivalent.

Version or named variant of the DNA extraction protocol used in this workflow, including any laboratory-specific modifications; use a stable string identifier such as 'standard_v1' or the kit protocol revision.
Primary lysis approach applied to release microbial DNA from the preserved sample during extraction; examples include bead_beating, enzymatic_lysis, chemical_lysis, or combined methods.

Amount of preserved reef material loaded into the extraction, reported as either mass in mg or volume in mL depending on sample type; record the value used at the start of extraction, typically within the kit's recommended range.
Final volume of buffer or water used to elute purified DNA from the extraction matrix, in microliters; record the volume used at the end of the extraction step, commonly 25 to 100 uL.

Measured concentration of extracted microbial DNA after elution, in ng/ul; record the concentration determined at the end of extraction using fluorometry or similar quantification, typically spanning 0.1 to >100 ng/ul.
Absorbance-based purity ratio (A260/A280) for the extracted DNA measured after extraction; typical values for acceptable DNA are around 1.7 to 2.0.

Outcome of the extraction negative control associated with this batch, recorded at the process level to indicate contamination status; use a categorical pass/fail style value based on control screening.

extracted_microbial_dna.reasoning: I fixed the collisions by removing the three duplicated field names that had already been generated elsewhere in the DAG. For extracted_microbial_dna, I kept only entity-level fields that remain distinct: source linkage, total yield, integrity/status, storage buffer, and storage location. I avoided reusing upstream process/QC measurements that were already emitted on the dna_extraction or other prior nodes, and I stayed within the entity territory by describing the DNA material rather than the extraction procedure.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the extracted DNA aliquot; use a stable string label such as 'DNA_GBR_S01_01' that identifies the purified DNA entity ready for amplification.
Identifier of the upstream preserved reef sample from which this DNA was extracted; use the same sample identifier format assigned at collection so the extraction can be traced to its source.

Total amount of purified DNA recovered from the extraction, in nanograms; record the yield for the DNA entity after elution, commonly spanning below 1 ng to several hundred ng depending on sample volume.
Simple assessment of DNA fragment integrity and suitability for amplification after extraction; use a categorical label based on QC review of the DNA entity.
Buffer or solution in which the extracted DNA is stored before amplification, if applicable; examples include nuclease-free water, TE buffer, or elution buffer.
Optional physical storage location for the extracted DNA aliquot within a freezer or cold storage unit, recorded as an operational string such as 'FZ2_R3_S12' to support sample retrieval.

Volume of the extracted DNA aliquot available for downstream library preparation, in microliters; record the aliquot amount at the time the DNA entity is set aside for amplification, typically 5 to 100 uL.

amplicon_library_preparation.reasoning: For the Process node amplicon_library_preparation, I included only library-preparation protocol details and process-level outputs that are not already captured elsewhere: target region, primer set, PCR conditions, indexing approach, and library QC indicators. I excluded DNA concentration, purity, and storage temperature because those fields were already generated for the extracted_microbial_dna entity and must not be repeated. I also excluded raw sequence file properties and sequencing instrument settings because those belong to downstream sequencing capture and signal nodes. The schema is focused on how the 16S amplicon library was created from extracted DNA and on minimal process outcome measures needed for reproducibility and batch tracking.

md_schema.descr: 16S rRNA gene region amplified for library preparation, recorded as the specific variable region or amplicon span targeted in this workflow, e.g. 'V3-V4', 'V4', or 'V4-V5'.
Forward primer sequence used to amplify the 16S target region during library preparation; record the exact nucleotide sequence used in the PCR reaction, written 5' to 3'.
Reverse primer sequence used to amplify the 16S target region during library preparation; record the exact nucleotide sequence used in the PCR reaction, written 5' to 3'.
Number of PCR amplification cycles used to generate the amplicon library from extracted DNA; record the cycle count applied during library preparation, typically 20 to 35 cycles.
PCR annealing temperature used during amplicon library preparation, in degrees Celsius; record the thermocycler setting used at the amplification stage, typically 50 to 68 C.
Expected size of the amplified 16S amplicon after library preparation, in base pairs; record the target fragment length implied by the primer set and protocol, typically 150 to 600 bp.
Strategy used to attach sample indices/barcodes during amplicon library preparation; use a categorical label describing the indexing design employed in this workflow.
Cleanup method used after amplification and indexing to remove primers, dimers, and small fragments; examples include bead_based_cleanup, gel_extraction, or column_cleanup.
Outcome of the no-template or negative PCR control associated with library preparation, recorded to indicate contamination status for the amplification batch.
Total mass of purified indexed amplicon library obtained after cleanup, in nanograms; record the yield at the end of library preparation, commonly used for pooling and sequencing input decisions.

sequencing_library.reasoning: For the Entity node sequencing_library, I included only intrinsic properties of the prepared indexed amplicon library itself: library identity, insert size, concentration, molarity, pooling readiness, and storage state. I excluded PCR and indexing protocol details because those belong to the upstream amplicon_library_preparation Process node, and I excluded sequencing instrument settings, run conditions, and raw read properties because those belong to the downstream sequencing_capture Capture node and raw_reads_fastq Signal node. I also avoided repeating any already_generated fields such as DNA concentration or storage temperature, keeping this schema focused on the final library as a material entity ready for sequencing.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared indexed 16S amplicon library aliquot; use a stable string such as 'LIB_GBR_S01_01' that labels the sequencing-ready library entity.
Identifier of the extracted microbial DNA entity used to create this library; record the upstream DNA sample reference so the library can be traced to its source material.
Measured concentration of the prepared sequencing library, in ng/ul; record the value obtained after cleanup and before pooling or loading, typically used to normalize libraries for sequencing.
Molar concentration of the sequencing library, in nM; record the converted library concentration used for pooling and instrument loading, often in the low nanomolar range.

Approximate insert size of the prepared amplicon library, in base pairs, excluding adapters and indices; record the expected fragment size distribution after preparation, typically around 250 to 550 bp for 16S amplicons.
Simple quality assessment of whether the prepared library meets the criteria for sequencing readiness, based on concentration, size distribution, and contamination screening.
Whether the library has been assigned to a sequencing pool or remains an individual unpooled aliquot at the time of metadata capture; record as an operational readiness attribute.
Storage condition for the prepared library before sequencing, such as frozen, chilled, or short-term ambient handling; record the maintained condition of the sequencing-ready entity.

Identifier or encoded label describing the adapter and index combination attached to this library, used to distinguish multiplexed samples in sequencing runs; use the exact operational label assigned by the lab or demultiplexing sheet.

water_condition_capture.reasoning: For the Capture node water_condition_capture, I included only the measurement-session and instrument-configuration details for the in situ environmental monitoring operation: the deployed sensor package, its manufacturer/model/serial information, calibration status, probe/channel settings, and the configured parameters used to capture water conditions. I did not include the actual environmental measurements themselves because those belong to the downstream Signal node site_environment_signal, and I avoided sample-origin or metadata-table fields because those belong to Entity/Derivative nodes. I also did not repeat any already_generated fields from other nodes. The schema is limited to what a downstream user needs to understand how the site water measurements were acquired and with which instrument setup.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the field instrument or sensor suite used to measure water conditions at the reef site; record the hardware vendor associated with the deployed measurement system.
Model name or number of the water-quality instrument or sensor suite used during capture; record the exact device model configured for in situ measurements.
Serial number of the deployed instrument or sensor module used for field capture; use the manufacturer-assigned serial string if available, e.g. 'SN12345678'.
Date and time when the in situ water-condition measurement session was performed at the sampling site and depth; record in ISO 8601 timestamp format such as '2024-07-18T09:30:00Z'.
Date of the most recent calibration performed on the sensor suite before the capture session, recorded as the calibration reference date used to validate field measurements.
Depth at which the water-condition capture was performed, in meters below the sea surface; record the sensor deployment depth for the measurement session, typically matching the sampling depth.
Duration of the water-condition measurement session at the site, in minutes; record how long the instrument was deployed or actively collecting readings for this capture event.

Configured temperature sensing mode or channel used during capture, if multiple modes or resolutions are available; record the operational setting applied to the instrument rather than the measured temperature value.
Configured pH probe or channel setting used during capture, if applicable; record the operational sensing mode or resolution used for the field measurement.
Configured salinity measurement mode or channel used during capture, if applicable; record the operational setting applied to the field instrument for salinity acquisition.

Field assay or sensor method used to capture nutrient concentrations at the sampling site, if performed as part of the session; record the operational assay design or instrument mode used for nutrient measurement.

Operator-assessed quality status of the capture session based on instrument function, calibration validity, and completeness of measurements; use a simple categorical status for the field acquisition event.

site_environment_signal.reasoning: For the Signal node site_environment_signal, I included only raw data-artefact descriptors: the signal identifier, source capture reference, file format, file size, dimensions, channel composition, and technical quality flags. I excluded the actual environmental sensor settings because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded the interpreted environmental table because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided duplicating site/sample identifiers already generated upstream except for the necessary linkage back to the capture event. The schema focuses on how the raw environmental observations are stored and assessed as data files or records.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw environmental signal record produced by the capture session; use a stable string such as 'ENV_SIG_GBR_S01_2024-07-18' to label the raw artefact.
Identifier of the upstream water-condition capture session that generated this raw environmental signal; use the same capture reference used in the field instrument log.
Digital format of the raw environmental data artefact, recorded at the time of acquisition or export; examples include 'csv', 'txt', 'json', or instrument-specific binary formats.
Size of the raw environmental data file in bytes, measured for the stored signal artefact after export; use the exact byte count of the raw record.
Count of individual measurement rows or samples contained in the raw environmental signal artefact, such as the number of time points or site-by-depth observations captured.
Count of distinct measured variables included in the raw signal, for example temperature, pH, salinity, and nutrient channels.
Technical completeness flag for the raw environmental signal, indicating whether all expected channels and records were successfully captured and exported.
Post-capture technical QC assessment of the raw environmental signal file, such as whether the record is usable without correction or requires re-export/recovery.
Path or repository location where the raw environmental signal is stored, recorded as a file path or accession string used for retrieval.

environment_metadata_table.reasoning: For the Derivative node environment_metadata_table, I included only computed/structured table properties and the algorithmic choices used to assemble the site-level environmental metadata: table identifier, join logic, aggregation/granularity, and summary dimensions. I excluded raw environmental file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded sequencing-derived community descriptors because those belong to later derivatives. I also avoided repeating site and sample identity fields already generated upstream unless needed as linkage keys for the table. The schema is focused on the assembled metadata product used for downstream joint analysis, not the raw measurements themselves.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the structured environmental metadata table; use a stable string such as 'ENV_META_GBR_2024' that labels the derivative table product.
Identifier of the raw environmental signal source used to construct this table; record the upstream signal reference so the derivative can be traced back to the measurement artefact.
Resolution at which the environmental metadata table is organized, describing the unit of one row in the derivative product; use a categorical label such as site-level or site-by-depth level.

Names of the fields used to join environmental observations with sampling descriptors when constructing the table, such as site code, depth, and date; record the operational join key names as a comma-separated string.
Number of rows in the assembled environmental metadata table, recorded after joining and structuring the input measurements; this describes the derivative table size.
Number of columns in the assembled environmental metadata table, recorded after structuring the input observations and descriptors; this describes the derivative table width.

Method used to summarize or consolidate repeated environmental observations during table construction, if applicable; examples include mean, median, or no aggregation when one row per site-depth exists.

Type of spatial descriptor included in the derivative table for each site, such as reef zone, GPS coordinate summary, or named sampling location; record the descriptor class represented in the table product.

Derivative-level QC flag indicating whether the assembled environmental metadata table is internally consistent and ready for downstream analysis, based on join completeness and expected column presence.

sequencing_capture.reasoning: For the Capture node sequencing_capture, I included only sequencing-run and instrument-configuration fields: instrument manufacturer/model/serial, run date, flow cell, chemistry, read length, lane/run identifiers, and actively configured settings that define how the amplicon library was read. I excluded library composition and indexing details because those belong to the upstream sequencing_library entity, and I excluded raw FASTQ properties because those belong to the downstream raw_reads_fastq signal. I also did not repeat any already-generated fields such as storage temperature or concentration. The schema is limited to the capture session and sequencer setup needed to reproduce the raw sequencing acquisition.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for the amplicon run; record the hardware vendor associated with the platform that generated the raw reads.
Model of the sequencing instrument used for the capture session; record the exact platform model, e.g. 'MiSeq', 'NextSeq 2000', or equivalent.
Instrument serial number for the sequencer used in this run; record the manufacturer-assigned serial string if available, e.g. 'MS123456'.
Date on which the sequencing capture session was performed, recorded in ISO date format (YYYY-MM-DD).
Sequencing run identifier assigned by the instrument or laboratory workflow, used to track the capture event and link raw reads to the run, e.g. 'RUN_2024_07_18_A'.
Flow cell or cartridge type used for the sequencing capture, recorded as the platform-specific consumable model or chemistry name.
Sequencing chemistry or kit version used for the run, recorded as the instrument-specific reagent chemistry, e.g. v2 or v3 chemistry identifiers.
Configured read length per read generated during the sequencing capture, in base pairs; record the nominal read length setting used for the run, such as 2x250 or 2x300.
Configured index read length used during the sequencing run, in base pairs; record the index read setting if multiplexed libraries were sequenced, typically 8 or 10 bp.
Library loading concentration used on the sequencer, in pM; record the concentration set at instrument loading time, typically in the low picomolar range.
Total duration of the sequencing capture session, in minutes; record the elapsed run time from start to completion of the read acquisition event.
Operator-assessed quality status of the sequencing capture session based on instrument performance and run completion; use a simple status for the run event.

raw_reads_fastq.reasoning: For the Signal node raw_reads_fastq, I removed field names that collided with earlier DAG steps and kept only raw-read artefact properties that had not already been generated under the same or equivalent names. I retained the FASTQ identifier, source run linkage, read count, pairing status, demultiplexing status, technical quality summary, and a storage reference field renamed to avoid collision. I excluded sequencing capture settings and downstream processing parameters because they belong to other nodes, and I avoided reusing file format, file size, read length, and generic storage location fields because those were already produced elsewhere in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw FASTQ artefact produced by the sequencing run; use a stable string such as 'FASTQ_GBR_S01_RUN1_R1' to label the data file or record.
Identifier of the upstream sequencing capture run that generated this raw FASTQ file; record the sequencing run reference used to link the file to its acquisition event.
Total number of sequencing reads contained in the raw FASTQ artefact after demultiplexing, recorded as the count of individual read entries in the file.
Whether the raw FASTQ artefact contains paired-end reads or single-end reads, reflecting the raw data structure produced by sequencing.
Flag indicating whether the raw reads were successfully separated by sample barcode/index into sample-specific FASTQ records at the time of file generation.
Technical quality summary of the raw FASTQ artefact, such as median or mean base-quality profile, captured as a stored QC descriptor for the raw signal.

Path, accession, or repository URI where the raw FASTQ artefact is stored for downstream processing and retrieval; use a storage reference distinct from earlier file-location fields, e.g. 's3://bucket/path/file.fastq.gz' or a local archive path.

read_processing.reasoning: For the Process node read_processing, I included only read-processing protocol settings and process-level outcome indicators: trimming and filtering software, version, repository, quality thresholds, adapter handling, read retention, and a batch QC flag. I excluded raw FASTQ properties such as file format, file size, read length, and storage location because those were already generated for the upstream signal and must not be repeated. I also excluded downstream denoising or ASV inference outputs because those belong to later nodes. The schema captures how reads were cleaned and what settings were used, not the properties of the input file or the resulting processed-read artefact itself.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software package used for read trimming, filtering, and demultiplexing in this step; record the exact tool name used for processing, e.g. 'dada2', 'cutadapt', or 'qiime2'.
Version of the processing software used for read cleanup, recorded at the time the reads were processed; use the exact release identifier, e.g. '1.30.0'.
Repository or distribution source for the read-processing software, such as a GitHub URL, Bioconductor package source, or package manager reference.
Number of bases trimmed from the left end of each read during processing, in base pairs; record the configured truncation/trimming setting applied before downstream analysis.
Number of bases trimmed from the right end of each read during processing, in base pairs; record the configured truncation/trimming setting applied before downstream analysis.
Maximum expected error threshold used to filter reads during processing; record the quality filtering cutoff applied to remove low-quality sequences.
Method used to remove adapters or primer remnants from reads during processing; examples include exact_match, local_alignment, or software-specific adapter clipping.
Minimum read length required for a read to be retained after trimming and filtering, in base pairs; record the cutoff applied during processing, typically set to exclude very short reads.
Proportion of raw reads retained after trimming, filtering, and demultiplexing, recorded as a process outcome indicator for the cleanup step.
Overall quality flag for the read-processing step based on adapter removal success, read retention, and expected quality thresholds; use a batch-level pass/warning/fail assessment.

processed_reads.reasoning: For the Signal node processed_reads, I kept only processed-read artefact descriptors that had not already been used elsewhere in the DAG. I retained identifiers, file format, size, retained read counts and lengths, QC summary, and a technical QC flag, while removing paired_end_status and storage_location because those collided with prior generated fields. I also excluded processing parameters, raw-file properties, and downstream inference settings, since those belong to other node types. The resulting schema describes the cleaned read signal as a stored technical artefact without duplicating earlier metadata fields.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the cleaned and quality-filtered read artefact produced by the read-processing step; use a stable string such as 'PROC_READS_GBR_S01_RUN1' to label the processed-read file.
Identifier of the upstream read-processing operation that produced this processed-read artefact; record the processing run reference used to link the file to its cleanup event.
Digital format of the cleaned read artefact at storage or export time; for this node record the processed read format, such as FASTQ, FASTQ.GZ, or other accepted container.
Size of the processed read file in bytes as stored after cleanup and export; record the exact byte count for the technical artefact.
Total number of reads retained after trimming, filtering, and demultiplexing, counted in the processed read artefact.
Typical or nominal length of reads in the processed-read artefact, in base pairs, after trimming and quality filtering; record the retained read length used for inference downstream.
Technical summary of quality filtering applied to the processed reads, such as average retained quality profile or a brief descriptor of the filtering outcome stored with the artefact.
Post-processing technical QC flag indicating whether the cleaned reads are suitable for downstream inference without further correction; use a simple categorical status for the processed signal.

feature_inference.reasoning: For the Process node feature_inference, I included only the inference algorithm and its key denoising parameters, along with process-level output quality indicators: software used, version, reference/source, truncation or error settings, chimera handling, and an inference QC flag. I excluded processed-read file properties such as pairing status and storage location because those belong to the upstream Signal node and must not be repeated. I also excluded the resulting ASV table properties because those belong to the downstream feature_table Derivative node. The schema focuses on how amplicon sequence variants were inferred from the processed reads, not on the input signal or the output table itself.

md_schema.descr: Name of the denoising or ASV inference software used in this step; record the exact tool used to infer amplicon sequence variants from processed reads, e.g. 'dada2', 'deblur', or 'qiime2'.
Version of the ASV inference software used for this process step; record the exact release or package version applied to the processed reads.
Repository or package source for the ASV inference software, such as a CRAN, Bioconductor, GitHub, or QIIME2 plugin reference.
Forward-read truncation length used during denoising, in base pairs; record the read position at which forward reads were truncated before ASV inference.
Reverse-read truncation length used during denoising, in base pairs; record the read position at which reverse reads were truncated before ASV inference.
Maximum expected error threshold applied to forward reads during denoising, used to control sequence quality before ASV inference.
Maximum expected error threshold applied to reverse reads during denoising, used to control sequence quality before ASV inference.
Method used to identify and remove chimeric sequences during ASV inference; examples include consensus, pooled, or de_novo approaches.
Minimum overlap required between paired reads for sequence merging during ASV inference, in base pairs; record this only if paired-end inference was performed.
Overall quality flag for the ASV inference step based on read retention, chimera handling, and convergence of denoising; use a batch-level pass/warning/fail assessment.

feature_table.reasoning: For the Derivative node feature_table, I included only properties of the computed ASV abundance table: table identity, source inference reference, table dimensions, sparsity, feature count, sample count, normalization state, and a table-level QC flag. I excluded denoising settings and software parameters because those belong to the upstream feature_inference Process node, and I excluded normalized-abundance properties because those belong to the downstream normalization node. I also avoided repeating sample identifiers or raw read properties already generated earlier. The schema is focused on the microbial community matrix as a computed result ready for downstream normalization and analysis.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the ASV abundance table derivative; use a stable string such as 'ASV_TABLE_GBR_2024' that labels the computed feature matrix.
Identifier of the upstream ASV inference process that generated this table; record the inference run reference used to trace the table back to denoised reads.
Number of samples represented as rows or columns in the ASV abundance table, depending on orientation; record the sample count present in the computed table.
Number of ASV features represented in the abundance table, recorded after inference and before any normalization or filtering performed downstream.
Orientation of the abundance matrix, indicating whether samples are represented in rows or columns; use the convention applied in this derivative product.
Fraction of zero-valued entries in the ASV abundance table, calculated from the computed matrix as a measure of community table sparsity.
Minimum sequencing depth observed among samples in the ASV table, recorded as the smallest total read count retained for any sample in the computed matrix.
Maximum sequencing depth observed among samples in the ASV table, recorded as the largest total read count retained for any sample in the computed matrix.
State of taxonomic annotation attached to the table, if any, describing whether ASVs are unlabeled or linked to reference taxonomy in the derivative product.
Derivative-level quality flag indicating whether the ASV abundance table is internally consistent and suitable for downstream normalization or ecological analysis.

normalization.reasoning: For the Process node normalization, I included only normalization-method details and process-level parameters used to transform the feature table: normalization software, version, repository, method, scaling target, zero handling, and a normalization QC flag. I excluded the raw feature-table dimensions and sparsity because those belong to the upstream Derivative node feature_table, and I excluded the normalized output table itself because that belongs to the downstream normalized_feature_table Derivative node. I also avoided repeating any previously generated identifiers or file-location fields. The schema focuses on how community abundances were made comparable across samples, not on the input matrix or the final normalized matrix.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or workflow used to normalize ASV abundances; record the exact tool applied in this step, e.g. 'qiime2', 'phyloseq', or a custom pipeline.
Version of the normalization software used for this process step; record the exact release or package version applied to the feature table.
Repository or package source for the normalization software, such as a GitHub URL, CRAN/Bioconductor package reference, or QIIME2 plugin source.
Method used to normalize community abundances across samples, chosen according to the workflow applied to the ASV table; record the transformation or scaling approach used.
Target sequencing depth or library size used when rarefying or scaling samples during normalization, reported as reads per sample; record the applied target used to make samples comparable.
Pseudocount added prior to log-ratio or compositional normalization, if used, recorded as the numeric offset applied to zero entries.
Strategy used to handle zero counts during normalization, if applicable; use a categorical label for the approach applied to the feature table.
Scale of the normalized abundance values produced by this process, such as proportions, log-ratios, or standardized values, recorded as the output representation targeted by the method.
Overall quality flag for the normalization step based on successful completion, sample retention, and absence of numerical issues; use a simple batch-level pass/warning/fail assessment.

normalized_feature_table.reasoning: For the Derivative node normalized_feature_table, I kept only fields that describe the normalized matrix itself without repeating identifiers already generated for earlier table-like nodes. I removed number_of_samples, number_of_features, and sparsity_fraction because they collided with fields already produced elsewhere in the DAG. The remaining fields focus on what makes this derivative distinct: its own identifier, provenance from the normalization run, value scale, row-sum behavior, transformation state, and QC status. I excluded process-level normalization settings and downstream joint-analysis outputs to stay within the derivative territory.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the normalized microbial community table; use a stable string such as 'NORM_TABLE_GBR_2024' that labels the analysis-ready derivative matrix.
Identifier of the upstream normalization process that generated this table; record the normalization run reference used to trace the derivative back to the raw ASV table.
Scale used for the normalized abundance values in the table, such as proportions, percentages, log-ratios, or standardized values; record the representation of the computed matrix.
Total abundance sum per sample row after normalization, recorded as a summary statistic of the computed matrix when applicable, typically near 1.0 for relative abundance tables.
Indication of whether the table values were transformed beyond scaling, such as log or compositional transforms, as part of the normalized derivative product.
Quality flag for the normalized table indicating whether the matrix is internally consistent and ready for downstream ecological or statistical analysis.

joint_analysis.reasoning: For the Process node joint_analysis, I included only analysis-model and integration parameters: the statistical framework used, version/repository, environmental variables included, community data transform choices, significance thresholds, and model/QC outcomes. I excluded normalized table dimensions and sparsity because those belong to the upstream normalized_feature_table Derivative node, and I excluded the resulting statistical outputs because those belong to the downstream community_environment_results Derivative node. I also avoided repeating any previously generated identifiers. The schema is limited to how the community and environmental data were combined and analyzed to assess spatial heterogeneity and coral-health-related patterns.

md_schema.descr: Name of the statistical or ecological analysis software used to integrate microbial community data with environmental metadata; record the exact tool or package used for the joint analysis, e.g. 'R', 'vegan', 'phyloseq', or a custom workflow.
Version of the software or package used for the joint analysis step; record the exact release applied to the normalized community table and environmental metadata.
Repository or package source for the joint-analysis software, such as a CRAN/Bioconductor reference, GitHub URL, or package manager source.
Primary statistical method used to assess relationships between community composition and environmental variables; choose the method matching the joint-analysis workflow used in this study.
Type of microbial input supplied to the joint analysis, recorded as the normalized abundance representation used in the model or ordination step.
Names of the environmental predictors included in the joint analysis, such as temperature, pH, salinity, nutrients, depth, or site descriptors; record the variable list used in the model.
Distance or dissimilarity metric used to compare microbial community profiles in the joint analysis, if applicable; examples include bray_curtis, jaccard, or euclidean.
P-value threshold applied to infer statistical significance in the joint analysis, recorded as the cutoff used for tests of association or model terms.
Method used to correct for multiple comparisons in the joint analysis, if applicable; use the statistical adjustment strategy applied to reported associations.

Overall quality flag for the joint analysis indicating whether the integration and statistical evaluation completed successfully and produced interpretable results; use a batch-level pass/warning/fail assessment.

community_environment_results.reasoning: For the Derivative node community_environment_results, I included only computed statistical-output descriptors: result table or figure identifiers, source analysis reference, output type, effect/association summaries, p-values, adjusted p-values, explained variance, model fit, and result-level QC. I excluded the joint-analysis method and software details because those belong to the upstream joint_analysis Process node, and I excluded raw or normalized community-table properties because those belong to earlier derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating site/sample identifiers except where needed as analysis linkage fields. The schema is focused on the integrated inference product that summarizes relationships between microbial community structure and environmental gradients.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the integrated statistical results product; use a stable string such as 'COMM_ENV_RES_GBR_2024' that labels the derivative output.
Identifier of the upstream joint-analysis process that produced these results; record the analysis run reference used to trace the output back to the integrated model.
Type of integrated statistical output produced by the analysis, such as model summary, ordination results, hypothesis test table, or association matrix.

Primary microbial community response represented in the integrated results, such as community composition, ASV structure, alpha diversity, or beta diversity; record the main ecological response summarized by the derivative.

Main environmental or spatial predictors evaluated in the integrated results, such as depth, site, temperature, pH, salinity, or nutrients; record the predictor set summarized by the derivative product.

Summary of the strength and direction of the association between microbial community patterns and predictors, reported as the effect size or correlation coefficient extracted from the integrated analysis.
Primary p-value or significance summary associated with the reported community-environment relationship, recorded at the derivative-output level.
Multiple-testing-adjusted p-value or significance summary associated with the reported result, if correction was applied during analysis.
Percentage of variation in microbial community structure explained by the integrated environmental or spatial model, reported as a derived statistical summary.
Model fit statistic reported with the integrated results, such as R-squared, pseudo-R-squared, or analogous fit measure used to summarize the derivative output.
Quality flag indicating whether the integrated results are statistically coherent, reproducible, and suitable for interpretation in the context of coral reef microbial heterogeneity analysis.
